name: The Regenerative Center
tagline: Neurosurgeon-led cell therapy, PRP and rehab under one roof in Paducah, Kentucky
description:
The Regenerative Center is a multi-specialty clinic at 2725 James Sanders Blvd in Paducah, Kentucky, registered with Medicare as Advancing Medical Solutions PSC. Dr. Matt Wallis, a chiropractor who founded IMAC Regeneration Center of Kentucky and grew that model to 15 clinics across five states, opened this practice in November 2023. Sean McDonald, MD, a neurosurgeon who moved into non-surgical spine and regenerative work, is the medical director and takes case reviews himself. Nine providers work on site across neurosurgery, chiropractic, physical therapy and nurse practitioner care, so most patients get rehab and structural care wrapped around whatever injection they come in for.

The cell work draws on three sources. Fat harvested from the patient under local anesthetic, bone marrow drawn from the hip, and mesenchymal cells from donated umbilical cord tissue. The clinic states it never uses embryonic cells. Delivery is either an image-guided injection placed with ultrasound or fluoroscopy for a joint, disc or nerve target, or an IV infusion where the target is systemic, which is how the neurological, autoimmune and lung protocols are run. PRP is sold on its own for orthopedic cases and hair restoration and is sometimes paired with cells.

Parkinson's is the condition the center leads with, and there is real history behind that. From December 2020 the Paducah practice at this address, then trading as IMAC Regeneration Center, was one of three sites in a Phase 1 study of umbilical cord derived mesenchymal cells for bradykinesia in Parkinson's disease, registered as NCT04385056 under an FDA-authorized IND. The center says Dr. McDonald was the lead physician administering it. That study has since closed and no trial is open here now, so anything offered today is elective, investigational and quoted privately after a free case review. The practice is also in the VA Community Care Network, though that referral route covers its non-opioid pain management, physical therapy and chiropractic care rather than cell therapy.

faqs.question: What kind of cells do you use?
faqs.answer: Mesenchymal cells from three sources. Fat taken from the patient under local anesthetic, bone marrow drawn from the hip, and tissue from screened donated umbilical cord. The clinic states it does not use embryonic cells.

faqs.question: Is this FDA-approved?
faqs.answer: No. Cell therapies are investigational and are not approved by the FDA for these uses. They are elective procedures and are not a replacement for standard medical care.

faqs.question: Was the Parkinson's clinical trial real?
faqs.answer: Yes. Phase 1 study NCT04385056 tested umbilical cord derived mesenchymal cells given by IV infusion for bradykinesia in Parkinson's disease, and the Paducah site at this address, then trading as IMAC Regeneration Center, was one of three locations. Dosing started in December 2020 and the study closed in 2022. The center says its current medical director led the dosing here. No study is open at the clinic now, so treatment you receive today is elective care rather than trial participation.

faqs.question: How are the cells given?
faqs.answer: Either as an image-guided injection placed with ultrasound or fluoroscopy when the target is a joint, disc or nerve, or as an IV infusion for the neurological, autoimmune and lung protocols.

faqs.question: Does insurance cover it?
faqs.answer: Partly. The clinic accepts most major insurance for the conventional side of what it does, meaning physician visits, physical therapy and chiropractic care. Cell therapy and PRP are cash-pay. Ask for the quote split into insurance lines and cash lines before you start.

faqs.question: Can veterans be treated here?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the VA Community Care Network, but the VA has to approve a referral first and the covered services are non-opioid pain management, physical therapy and chiropractic rather than cell therapy. Ask your VA primary care provider to refer to Advancing Medical Solutions, NPI 1699454249.

faqs.question: How much does it cost?
faqs.answer: Nothing is published. The center runs a free case review by phone, video chat or in person and quotes each plan afterward, so the figure depends on the cell source, how many sites are treated and whether the protocol is one injection or a course of infusions.

costPage.introEmpty: The Regenerative Center publishes no price list. The free case review comes first, by phone, video chat or in person, and the quote follows once a provider has looked at your imaging and history. What you pay turns on how much of the plan is cell therapy or PRP, which is cash-pay, and how much is physical therapy, chiropractic and physician visits, which the clinic bills to most major insurers. Ask for that split in writing before you commit to anything.

items.label: Case review and evaluation
items.note: Advertised as complimentary and offered by phone, video chat or in person with the medical director.

items.label: Stem cell therapy from your own fat or bone marrow
items.note: Quoted after the case review. The harvest is done in office under local anesthetic, so the fee covers collection, processing and the image-guided injection.

items.label: Umbilical cord derived cell therapy
items.note: Donor tissue is bought in, so this line prices differently from harvesting your own cells. Ask which product is being used and at what dose.

items.label: IV cell infusion for neurological, autoimmune or lung conditions
items.note: Systemic protocols are often more than one infusion. Ask how many are inside the quoted number and what a repeat would cost.

items.label: PRP injection
items.note: Sold on its own for joints, discs and hair restoration. Cheaper than cell therapy and often the first step offered.

items.label: Physical therapy, chiropractic and physician visits
items.note: The side of the practice billed to most major insurers, so your cost here is a copay and deductible rather than a cash price.

items.label: Hormone therapy, peptides and medical weight loss
items.note: Separate ongoing programs with their own monthly cost. They sit outside any cell therapy quote.

faqs.question: How much does The Regenerative Center cost?
faqs.answer: There is no published figure. Cell therapy and PRP are quoted per plan after the free case review, and the number moves with the cell source, how many sites are treated and whether the protocol is a single injection or a course of infusions. The rehab and physician side is billed to insurance instead, so ask for the quote split into cash lines and insurance lines.

faqs.question: Is the first appointment free?
faqs.answer: The case review is advertised as complimentary and can be done by phone, video chat or in person. Any imaging you do not already have is a separate cost.

faqs.question: Will insurance pay for stem cell therapy here?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. Cell therapy is elective and investigational, and insurers do not cover it. What the clinic bills to insurance is the physical therapy, chiropractic and physician visits around the procedure.

faqs.question: Is there a veterans route?
faqs.answer: Yes, but a limited one. The practice takes VA Community Care Network referrals for non-opioid pain management, physical therapy and chiropractic, with VA approval needed first. Cell therapy is not part of that route.
